first.rationale: Current situation shows activation down 6% QoQ and competitor pressure on price-sensitive SMB. Memory_73 established promotional pricing works for SMB acquisition; memory_31 showed onboarding simplification works but addresses a secondary symptom. Verification of memory_73's revenue quality and memory_31's durability will clarify whether pricing or activation messaging is the leverage point. However, promotional_pricing carries downstream risk to margin structure and reference pricing if overused—hence the small_guarded_test scale. This preserves optionality: if competitor pricing stabilizes or if verification shows activation messaging has better unit economics, we pivot. Memory_57 (referral incentives) is deprioritized because it targets established customers, not the acute competitive threat to new SMB acquisition.

final.rationale: Archive verification reveals critical finding: memory_73's promotional pricing caused -12% retention on acquired cohort, making it unsustainable despite +18% revenue lift. This directly contradicts the objective of maximizing sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Memory_31 confirmed signup simplification works durably on SMB (+4% qualified revenue, only -1% retention). Combined with memory_91 (activation messaging improved week-one engagement), activation_messaging is the only lever that addresses the 6% activation decline and 4% onboarding completion decline WITHOUT introducing churn risk. Referral incentives (memory_57) require existing customer base to be healthy first. Enterprise sales assist does not address the core SMB activation problem. Standard_experiment scale allows confident measurement of messaging impact on both activation and early retention, informing whether the decline is messaging-addressable or signals deeper product friction.
